headline: High: LangGraph’s default write/network orchestration can amplify dbt-core outputs into unsafe actions, while shared workspace and broad egress create medium leakage and conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core is an open-source data-engineering tool with allowlisted egress and data-warehouse I/O, while LangGraph can wire developer-defined tools and nodes with stdin/stdout and filesystem access. No shared channel is explicit, so direct injection is not proven; the plausible bridge is manual or application-defined content flow, which is lower severity.
conditions: IF the operator wires dbt-core outputs into a LangGraph node as trusted text
IF LangGraph nodes parse dbt-generated files or stdout as instructions
mitigations: Add a strict schema parser for dbt outputs
Separate instruction text from data payloads
Disable automatic execution of parsed content
Review any file-to-prompt bridge before deployment

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, and LangGraph can read/write application-defined files while sending context to model providers and developer-defined tools. A shared workspace or file handoff would expose warehouse data to broader egress paths in default orchestration, so leakage is plausible even though the exact pipeline is not documented.
conditions: IF dbt artifacts or warehouse extracts are placed in LangGraph-accessible files
IF LangGraph forwards those files or context to external model providers
mitigations: Keep dbt artifacts in a separate directory
Redact sensitive columns before handoff
Restrict LangGraph tool inputs to summaries only
Turn off unnecessary file reads in the graph
Use a local-only model for sensitive runs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can call a data warehouse, and LangGraph can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, write files, and use broad network egress. Even without explicit git or shared-lock support, overlapping write and network authority over shared resources creates a realistic conflict pathway in default orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents target the same workspace or downstream warehouse objects
IF LangGraph nodes mutate files that dbt also reads or writes
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize access to shared artifacts
Use per-run temp directories
Add file-locking around shared outputs
Avoid concurrent writes to the same warehouse objects

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can produce transformed data and artifacts that LangGraph may treat as node inputs or tool outputs. Because LangGraph can take actions through developer-defined tools and broad egress, an unverified dbt result can cascade into irreversible downstream actions or external calls in default configurations.
conditions: IF LangGraph uses dbt-produced tables, manifests, or logs as authoritative inputs
IF downstream LangGraph tools send actions or messages based on those inputs
mitigations: Insert a human review step before actions
Require validation against source data
Block action tools until checks pass
Log provenance for every dbt-derived field
Use dry-run mode for downstream steps

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches warehouse data, while LangGraph handles model-provider API keys and broad egress. The pair can move the same regulated data class from a warehouse into third-party model calls, creating retention and residency mismatch risk even though no specific certification gap is documented for either agent.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is included in LangGraph prompts or tool inputs
IF the model provider or tool endpoint stores or processes that data outside approved regions
mitigations: Classify the data before each run
Exclude regulated rows from prompts
Use region-locked providers
Set short retention on logs
Document a DPA and residency review
